subject_session: AN: 85 fibers/47 animals (example sub-G150805 unit1); Cortex: 000986 sub-LA8 ses-1, 192 units

headline_stat.name: STRF-CF vs published-BF correlation (log space, n=85)

stated_limitation: No stimulus waveforms are stored, so reverse correlation against a continuous stimulus is not possible; the tone-pip map is the appropriate estimator here.

justification.dataset: Two appropriate auditory datasets used with an explicit, defensible reframing to tone-pip STRFs since no DANDI dataset stores the rich stimulus waveforms a full reverse-correlation STRF requires.
justification.handling: Real remfile-streamed data with correct per-sweep tone-onset alignment, NaN handling, explicit level/rep/frequency inclusion gates, and vectorized perievent extraction for cortex.
justification.analysis: Baseline-subtracted per-frequency PSTH STRFs with Wilcoxon/Kruskal significance and a strong CF-vs-published-BF validation; no explicit shuffle null for the maps and a coarse 1ms-quantized latency metric keep it just short of ideal.
justification.correctness: Every headline number (r=0.994, n=85, 47 animals, bw 0.46 oct, latency medians 4.5/17 ms) reproduces exactly from the committed CSV, is internally consistent with figures, and is physically plausible.
justification.figures: Five clear, unit-labeled figures with sample sizes, a tonotopic gallery, population summaries, and a legible periphery-vs-cortex latency comparison that shows the effect directly.
justification.honesty: The write-up is proportionate throughout, plainly flagging the tone-pip approximation, restricting the weak latency-CF trend with its actual p-value, and noting the coarse cortical frequency axis and single session.
